from z3 import *

v = 9
b = 36
r = 12
k = 3
lam = 3

X = [[Bool(f"x_{i}_{j}") for j in range(b)] for i in range(v)]

s = Solver()

# Every row sums to r
for i in range(v):
    s.add(PbEq([(X[i][j], 1) for j in range(b)], r))

# Every column sums to k
for j in range(b):
    s.add(PbEq([(X[i][j], 1) for i in range(v)], k))

# Every pair of distinct rows has inner product lam
for i1 in range(v):
    for i2 in range(i1 + 1, v):
        s.add(PbEq([(And(X[i1][j], X[i2][j]), 1) for j in range(b)], lam))

# Symmetry breaking:
# Sort columns lexicographically to reduce search space
for j in range(b - 1):
    # Column j >= Column j+1
    # We can implement this by comparing the columns as binary numbers
    conds = []
    for i in range(v):
        # If all previous elements are equal, then X[i][j] >= X[i][j+1]
        eqs = [X[k][j] == X[k][j+1] for k in range(i)]
        conds.append(Implies(And(eqs) if eqs else True, X[i][j] >= X[i][j+1]))
    s.add(And(conds))

print("Solving...")
if s.check() == sat:
    m = s.model()
    res = []
    for i in range(v):
        for j in range(b):
            res.append(1 if is_true(m[X[i][j]]) else 0)
    print("SAT")
    print(res)
else:
    print("UNSAT")
